rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE DESPINA N. KOKALIS REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST DATED MAY 13, 1993, AS AMENDED
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR Demurrer To First Amended Petition For Trust Contest To Set Aside And Terminate Trust, Based Upon 1) Foregery/Invalidity Of Will 2) Fraud And Concealment To Appropriate Entire Estate Of Nicholas Kokalis As No Assets Belong To The Disinherited Despina Kokalis' Living Trust (Added For Posting Of Tentative Ruling)
rulings.Rulings: [Part 3 of 4] Petitioner's forgery allegations do not change the general rule, either. The FAP alleges that the 1969 Will was forged, but there is no allegation that anyone sought to probate the 1969 Will or sought to use it in any way to acquire assets from Nicholas' estate. Instead, the OP alleged that Despina Kokalis and Angeliki failed to probate Nicholas' will. (OP, paragraph 11(a).) The mere creation and delivery of a forged will, without any allegation that it was ever used to acquire assets or cause injury, does not support any cognizable cause of action, let alone grounds to contest a separate Trust. Similarly, the fraud allegations fail to allege cognizable damages or injury. Certainly, the presentation of a forged will (after concealing it for seven years) may constitute a misrepresentation of material fact. But Petitioner does not allege how she was "disinherited" or otherwise injured by virtue of that misrepresentation or delay in producing a copy of the non-probated will. Alternatively, even if the FAP does allege sufficient harm or injury, the Fraud claim appears to be time-barred based on the face of the pleading. Each of the fraudulent acts or alleged breaches appear to have occurred and have been known to Petitioner more than thirty (30) years ago. The alleged "concealment" ended in 1993 when Petitioner received a copy of the will. (FAC, paragraph 27.) The FAP also alleges that Despina failed to provide a "Full Accounting of the Nicholas Kokalis Estate Assets, including Real Estate Assets, Bank Statements, Income and Expenses for Seven Years after Nicholas Kokalis death." (FAP, paragraph 30(b).) There is no allegation that Despina was appointed or acted as a personal representative of Nicholas' estate Even if Despina had a duty to provide such an accounting, the alleged breach occurred from 1986 to 1993. The FAP contains a conclusory statement that the "above wrongful conduct" or "above inheritance theft" was not discovered by Petitioner until November 20, 2025, when she received notice of Angeliki's Petition for Order to Confirm Trust Assets. (FAC, paragraphs 29, 33.) But the FAP fails to identify which of the "above conduct" was not discovered until then. Instead, as discussed, the material allegations of misconduct were based on acts or omissions that occurred and were known to Petitioner by 1993. The alleged fraudulent actions - forgery, and concealment of the forgery - all predate the 2025 filing by decades. The FAP does not allege how or what the 2025 filing revealed to Petitioner about the alleged fraudulent actions that the 1993 delivery of the 1969 Will did not. Fraud claims must be alleged with particularity. The FAC does not allege a particular fraud that was not discovered or discoverable beyond the limitations period. The FAP further alleges that Despina and/or Angeliki breached a duty to Petitioner by: transferring an interest in certain property in violation of "paragraph FIFTH (f)" of the Will. (FAP, paragraph 31); making prohibited transfers of estate asset to "beneficiaries" and by "[c]hanging the testamentary intent in the Will by reducing [Petitioner's] one third share to "$10,000." (FAC, paragraphs 30(c) and (d); and 31.) The FAP's allegations lurch between asserting the 1969 Will and contingent testamentary trust reflect Decedent's testamentary intent to leave certain real property in equal shares to his three children (see paragraphs 15, 30, 31, 35), and asserting that the 1969 Will is a forgery created by Respondents (see paragraphs 1, 10, 11, 13, 14, 17, 20, 21, 24, 32, 36, 37, 39). Sometimes these allegations are made within the same paragraph (see paragraphs 27, 29).

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE DESPINA N. KOKALIS REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST DATED MAY 13, 1993, AS AMENDED
rulings.Calendar Matter: Demurrer To First Amended Petition For Trust Contest To Set Aside And Terminate Trust, Based Upon 1) Foregery/Invalidity Of Will 2) Fraud And Concealment To Appropriate Entire Estate Of Nicholas Kokalis As No Assets Belong To The Disinherited Despina Kokalis' Living Trust
rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 4] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Michael B. McNaughton. PARTIES TO APPEAR. The parties are ordered to appear at the hearing, to address the issues the court raises in this tentative ruling and to address whether there is a basis to grant leave to amend the pleading. Before the court is Respondent Angeliki Nicholas Kokaliszarikos' Demurrer To Maria Sotiras' First Amended Petition For Trust Contest To Set Aside And Terminate Trust, Based Upon (1) Forgery /Invalidity Of Will (2) Fraud And Concealment To Appropriate Entire Estate Of Nicholas Kokalis, As No Assets Belong To The Disinherited Despina Kokalis' Living Trust, Dated May 13, 1993, Seeking Damages For Converting Property Belonging To Nicholas Kokalis' Three Beneficiary Children ("Demurrer"). Petitioner demurs generally to the First Amended Petition ("FAP") under Code of Civil Procedure sec. 430.10(e), on grounds that it 1) is a sham pleading, contradicting the allegations pleaded in the initial petition regarding the Will's validity; 2) fails to overcome or plead around the documents attached to the FAP and subject to the Demurrer's request for judicial notice; and 3) the fraud claim is not plead with particularity and is otherwise time barred. Respondent's request for the court to take judicial notice of certain records - a certified certificate of death for Despina N. Kokalis, four joint tenancy deeds, four declarations re death of joint tenant recorded on July 25, 1986, and Petitioner's initial, prior petition - is GRANTED, pursuant to Evidence Code sections 452 and 453. The court notes, judicial notice is limited to the relevant facts properly subject to notice given the materials presented and does not, for example, extend to the truth of assertions in those materials. (See Richtek USA, Inc. v. UPI Semiconductor Corp. (2015) 242 Cal.App.4th 651, 659-660.) The Demurrer is SUSTAINED, as follows. A demurrer challenges the legal sufficiency of an opponent's pleading, based on defects that appear either on the face of the pleading under attack or from matters outside the pleading that are judicially noticeable. (See Blank v. Kirwan (1985) 39 Cal.3d 311, 318; County of Fresno v. Shelton (1998) 66 Cal.App.4th 996, 1008, 1009.) A general demurrer is appropriate where there is a defect or defense that will defeat the claimed right to recover in whole or in part, or which discloses a complete defense, apparent on the face of the pleading or from any matter of which the court must or may take judicial notice. (See, e.g., Cnty. of San Bernardino v. Superior Ct. (2022) 77 Cal. App. 5th 1100, 1107; Casterson v. Superior Ct. (2002) 101 Cal. App. 4th 177, 183.) Demurrers challenge only the legal sufficiency of pleadings on their face, not the truth or adequacy of factual allegations or evidence (Code of Civil Proc. sec. 430.30(a)). A ruling on a demurrer does not determine contested factual issues relating to the merits. It is improper to sustain a demurrer without leave to amend where the essential defect of the complaint lies in poor pleading, not in lack of facts. (see, e.g. M. G. Chamberlain & Co. v. Simpson (1959) 173 Cal. App. 2d 263, 267) "[I]f, on consideration of all facts stated, it appears that plaintiff is entitled to any relief against defendant, complaint will be held good, though facts may not be clearly stated, or may be intermingled with statement of other facts irrelevant to cause of action shown, or though plaintiff may demand relief to which he is not entitled under facts alleged." (Augustine v. Trucco (1954) 124 Cal.App.2d 229, 236.)

rulings.Rulings: [Part 4 of 4] The Opposition argues Petitioner is allowed to plead alternate and inconsistent claims. That is true. But Petitioner cannot make contradictory allegations within alternate claims. On the face of the FAP, the allegation are not pleaded as distinct alternative or inconsistent legal theories. Instead, Petitioner seeks the best of both worlds to the extent she seeks to void an allegedly forged will while at the same time attempting to enforce selected terms contained in it. The FAP contains various other allegations which are intermingled with the fraud and forgery claims. None are sufficient to cure the above defects or to state facts that would support grounds to invalidate or set aside Despina's separate Trust. Though unclear, it appears from the allegations that Petitioner may not be seeking to set aside Despina's Trust, after all. Rather, Petitioner may be claiming that certain assets held by Angeliki, Despina and/or her Trust really belong to Nicholas' non-probated estate and that Maria may be entitled to some share of that estate as a potential intestate heir. (See, FAP, Prayer for Relief, paragraphs 2, 3, and 4.) If that is the case, a Petition to invalidate a separate Trust is not the correct vehicle. Whatever the correct vehicle may be, it will have its own procedural and pleading requirements, elements of proof, standing issues, statute of limitations, and other potential defenses. This Court expresses no advice or opinion as to the form or merits of any such alternative petition, claim, or other procedure. On this general demurrer, the Court rules that the FAP, just like the OP, fails to state facts sufficient to constitute a cause of action that would be grounds to support a Petition to For Trust Contest. rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE DESPINA N. KOKALIS REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST DATED MAY 13, 1993, AS AMENDED
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR Demurrer To First Amended Petition For Trust Contest To Set Aside And Terminate Trust, Based Upon 1) Foregery/Invalidity Of Will 2) Fraud And Concealment To Appropriate Entire Estate Of Nicholas Kokalis As No Assets Belong To The Disinherited Despina Kokalis' Living Trust (Added For Posting Of Tentative Ruling)
rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 2] The FAP is entitled a "contest to set aside and terminate" a trust established by Despina Kokalis, dated May 13, 1993 (the "Trust"). Despina Kokalis was married to Nicholas Kokalis until he died on March 23, 1986. Despina died on March 8, 2025. Petitioner, along with her brother George Kokalis, are the issue of Nicholas Kokalis from a former marriage. Respondent Angeliki Kokalis is the daughter of both Nicholas and Despina. (FAP, paragraphs 2,3, 4.) The original Petition ("OP") was filed on January 29, 2026. In it, Petitioner sought to contest and set aside Despina's Trust on the grounds that it disposes of the Trust assets in a way that is inconsistent with Nicholas' intentions as expressed in his will dated September 10, 1969 which, according to Petitioner, was to leave one third of Nicholas' estate to each of his three children. (OP, paragraph 8.) This Court sustained a demurrer with leave to amend because, among other things: (1) The OP failed to state facts that would establish a duty on Despina to provide for all of Nicholas' children equally in her Trust; and (2) Nicholas' 1969 Will, on its face, did not create such a duty because it provided for his children only in the event that Despina predeceased him (which she did not) and provided that his entire estate would go to his wife Despina if she survived him (which she did). As stated in the Order sustaining demurrer, the OP failed "to state facts sufficient to establish Petitioner's entitlement to any distribution or other interest under the 1969 Will or any damages proximately caused by either Despina or Angelika." This Court's prior Order sustaining demurrer to the initial petition was issued with leave to amend in part to allow Petitioner to plead around the contingent terms of the 1969 Will, and explain how Respondents owed her a fiduciary duty under the 1969 Will. The FAP now seeks to contest the Trust on theories of "Forgery" and "Fraud." Under its First Cause of Action (entitled, "Contest of Will (Forgery)", Petitioner alleges the 1969 Will is not valid because it was "not signed by the Decedent" and that, "as a direct result of his forgery, Plaintiff has been deprived of his rightful inheritance." (FAP, paragraphs 17, 18.) Under its Second Cause of Action (entitled "Fraud"), the FAP alleges that Despina defrauded Petitioner by falsely representing that the 1969 Will was valid and by concealing a copy of the Will for seven years (between 1986 and 1993). (FAP, paragraphs, 24 - 27.) Paragraph 27 alleges (among other things) that Despina's Trust "should be terminated for her forgery of [Nicholas's Will], [] [and because] she failed to provide a copy of the Original Will to Petitioner, concealed the same, for over seven (7) years, so as to allow Defendant to accomplish her goals to prevent Petitioner from adequately verifying [Nicholas'] estate documents [] until seven years after his death in 1993. [] This substantial delay was to cement full concealment of the Will and to allow [Despina] to take improper steps to appropriate the assets by this forged Will." Neither the Forgery nor Fraud allegations are sufficient "to set aside or terminate" Despina's Trust. Nor do they establish a duty on Despina to re-write her Trust in conformity with Nicholas' desires, whether expressed in the 1969 Will or otherwise. Generally, a trustor has a right to dispose of trust assets any way he or she chooses. The FAC alleges no facts that would alter that general rule. Despina survived Nicholas by almost 39 years. (FAC paragraphs 4, 8.) She had a right to create her own estate plan and name her own beneficiaries regardless of what her former husband may have desired.
